voyage.name: St Jean Cathedral
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 08:15-12:00, 13:45-19:30, Sat Sun 08:15-12:00, 13:45-19:00; services (no visits) Mon-Fri 09:00 and 19:00, Sat 09:00, Sun 08:30 and 10:30 (high mass)
voyage.content: The cathedral is dedicated to St John the Baptist (St Jean-Baptiste) and St Stephen (St Etienne) and has the title of primatiale because the Bishop of Lyon has the honorary title of Primat des Gaules. Built between 1180 and 1480, it is mostly of Gothic style with Romanesque elements; the oldest parts are the chancel and the lateral chapels, and as one goes towards the façade, the style becomes more and more Gothic. T

voyage.name: St Jean archaeological garden
voyage.address: rue de la Bombarde/rue Mandelot/rue des Estrées
voyage.content: Next to St Jean cathedral (on the northern side), this small garden shows the remains of the religious buildings which occupied the site before the cathedral was erected. The oldest remains date back to the 4th century (baptistery of the former St Etienne church).

voyage.name: Traboules
voyage.content: The traboules are a typical architectural feature of Lyon's historical buildings. They are corridors which link two streets through a building, and usually a courtyard. Many traboules are unique architectural masterpieces, largely influenced by Italy and especially Florence.Some of them are officially open to the public. They link the following addresses:- 54 rue St Jean <> 27 rue du Boeuf (the longest in Lyon)- 27 r

voyage.name: Renaissance courtyards
voyage.content: Besides the buildings cited above, some have very beautiful courtyards but no real traboules (that is to say, no crossing from one street to another). The most outstanding are: Maison du Chamarier (37 rue St Jean) and Maison du Crible (16 rue du Boeuf), in which stands the famous "Pink Tower".

voyage.name: Rue St Jean
voyage.content: This cobblestone pedestrian street is the main axis of the area. It is full of souvenir shops and restaurants mainly intended for tourists. Local people are aware that real good bouchons are extremely rare here. On a sunny Sunday afternoon, it may be hard to walk because of the crowd of both locals and tourists. You can also check out the more quiet rue des Trois Maries which runs parallel to rue St Jean, between pla

voyage.name: Rue du Boeuf
voyage.content: Parallel to Rue St Jean, this street is much more quiet and just as beautiful. It also has a number of restaurants, more expensive than in rue St Jean but, on average, much more worth the money.

voyage.name: Place du Change
voyage.content: The largest square in the area has two remarkable buildings. The Loge du Change, on the west side, was partially built by the great architect Soufflot. It is now a Protestant church known as Temple du Change. It can be visited on Saturdays. Religious services on Sundays, 10:30. Opposite is the Maison Thomassin, with its Gothic-style 14th-century façade. The Thomassins were a powerful merchant family in the Renaissanc

voyage.name: Rue Juiverie
voyage.content: Another typical street of Vieux Lyon. It is named after the Jewish community who settled there but were expelled in the 14th century. Check out the back courtyard at Hôtel Builloud (number 8); it has a magnificent gallery on the first floor, designed by Philibert Delorme who was one of the most prominent local architects during the Renaissance.

voyage.name: St Paul church
voyage.content: A very nice church, with mixed Romanesque and Gothic styles. The oldest parts are from the 10th century.

voyage.name: St Georges neighbourhood
voyage.address: rue St Georges, rue du Doyenné and other smaller streets
voyage.content: St Georges is the name given to the south part of the Vieux Lyon. It has nice Renaissance buildings which, however, do not really compare to the palaces of St Jean; on the other hand, it is much more quiet than the St Jean area.

voyage.name: Montée du Gourguillon
voyage.content: This picturesque montée (sloping street on hillside) starts behind Vieux Lyon metro station and ends quite close to the Roman theatres of Fourvière. It was the main link between the river Saône and the top of Fourvière throughout the Roman era, Middle Ages and Renaissance. Nowadays it keeps a medieval spirit. Around numbers 5-7 is Impasse Turquet, a small cul-de-sac named after Etienne Turquet, an Italian who is said

voyage.name: Palais de Justice
voyage.content: The historical court house, also named "the 24 columns", was built between 1835 and 1842 by architect Louis-Pierre Baltard. It is a fine example of French "neo-classical" architecture. It now hosts only the criminal court (Cour d'Assises) and the court of appeal. The other jurisdictions moved to a new building in Part-Dieu in 1995. The most famous trial held there was that of the former head of the Lyon Gestapo, Klau

voyage.name: Fourvière basilica
voyage.content: Built in 1872 and dedicated to the Virgin Mary, patron saint of Lyon, this massive church made of white marble has been compared to an elephant with its feet up. It is a typical example of the 19th century "eclectic" style, with architectural elements recalling antique, classical and Gothic eras. The Byzantine-style interior decoration is extremely exuberant, too much so for some people. Tours of the roof and bell to

voyage.name: Musee d'art religieux
voyage.hours: Daily 10:00-12:30 and 14:00-17:30, closed in January and February
voyage.content: The small museum holds treasures donated to the church for its construction.

voyage.name: Esplanade de Fourvière
voyage.content: Next to the basilica is the panoramic viewpoint, with the best view over the city. If the weather is clear, Mont Blanc can be seen in the distance. This is a very good point to start your visit of the city because you can really see its general layout.

voyage.name: Metallic tower of Fourvière
voyage.content: Next to the basilica stands a smaller (86 m, 282 ft) replica of the Eiffel Tower, completed in 1894. Its construction was supported by anticlerical people in order to have a non-religious building as the highest point in Lyon, which it actually is with an altitude of 372 m (1272 ft) at the top. It now serves as a radio and TV antenna and is closed to the public.

voyage.name: Roman theatres
voyage.content: These two well-preserved theatres are the most important remnant of the Roman city of Lugdunum. The Gallo-Roman museum was built next to them. The summer festival "Nuits de Fourvière" takes place here every year, which may cause access restrictions in the evening from June to early August.

voyage.name: St Irénée church
voyage.hours: Church 08:30-18:00 daily, crypt Sat 14:30-17:00, closed in Aug
voyage.content: The oldest church in Lyon, and one of the oldest in France. The site is built on a Gallo-Roman necropolis which was in use for centuries, until the Middle Ages. Some sarcophagi from the 5th or 6th century are visible in the courtyard. The crypt dates back to the 9th century and was renovated in the 19th century. Early Christian remains (from the 4th-6th centuries) are kept inside. The church was rebuilt in the 19th c

voyage.name: Amphithéâtre des Trois Gaules
voyage.content: This Roman theatre is the place where the first Christian martyrs of Gaul were killed. Documents say that it was the largest theatre in Gaul at that time, but nobody knows exactly how far it extends under the neighbouring buildings, nor what remains from the Roman era after centuries of construction. After the closing of the old Fine Arts school (the grey building overlooking the theatre), a debate was initiated abou

voyage.name: Église du Bon-Pasteur
voyage.content: 19th-century Romanesque church unique for not having a front entrance due to construction conflicts with the barracks across the street.

voyage.name: Montée de la Grande Côte
voyage.content: This steep street has Renaissance buildings and offers a very beautiful view over the city from its top.

voyage.name: Croix-Rousse traboules
voyage.content: Look for the lanterns over the doors and the specific signs.

voyage.name: Mur des Canuts
voyage.content: This painted wall is dedicated to the history and typical architecture of the Croix-Rousse hill.

voyage.name: Church of Saint-Bruno des Chartreux
voyage.content: The only Baroque church in Lyon. The interior is magnificent, especially the altar (by Servandoni, modified by Soufflot, 18th century) and the canopy (by Servandoni).

voyage.name: Jardin Rosa Mir
voyage.content: This amazing garden was built by a Spanish refugee, Jules Senis, and dedicated to his mother. Senis had cancer and had made the vow of building this garden if he ever came out of the hospital; fortunately, he did. The garden is a fine mixture of mineral and vegetal elements, in a style influenced by Gaudi's works in Barcelona.

voyage.name: Place des Terreaux
voyage.content: This large square was completely redesigned in the 1990s by the artist Daniel Buren. On the East side stands the City Hall. On the North side, you will find the fountain sculpted by Bartholdi, the 'father' of the Statue of Liberty; this fountain was moved from the West side when the square was renovated. It now faces Palais St Pierre, which hosts the Museum of Fine Arts.

voyage.name: City Hall
voyage.address: place des Terreaux and place de la Comédie
voyage.content: The city hall, built in the 17th century, has a very beautiful façade on Place des Terreaux. The most notable feature of this façade is the sculpture representing King Henri IV on horseback (in the middle of the upper part). Unfortunately, it is impossible to visit the building except during the "Heritage days" (Journées du patrimoine) in mid-September.

voyage.name: Opera house
voyage.content: Opposite the City Hall stands the opera house. The 1826 theatre built by Chenavard and Pollet was completely redesigned by Jean Nouvel who kept only the façades and the foyer on the first floor. The building was reopened in 1993. The history of these works was epic: a lot of technical problems occurred and the final cost of the project was six times the initial estimate. Today, the glass top has become a classical la

voyage.name: Mur des Lyonnais
voyage.content: This impressive painted wall portraits some of the most famous people who were born in Lyon, from Renaissance poet Louise Labé to the Lumière brothers, the inventors of cinema, to chef Paul Bocuse.

voyage.name: Place Sathonay
voyage.content: A charming neighbourhood square planted with old plane trees. Just sit at a terrace, watch the locals playing pétanque and enjoy the mood.

voyage.name: Saint-Nizier Church
voyage.content: Very nice church of flaming Gothic style.

voyage.name: Rue Mercière
voyage.content: This cobblestone pedestrian street is the only significant remain from the Renaissance in Presqu'île. The name of the street refers to the clothing industry. There are traboules connecting the street to the buildings on the Saône bank. The street hosts very numerous restaurants which are far from being all good.

voyage.name: Place des Jacobins
voyage.content: The state of this square is typical of the "automobile-friendly" urban planning of the 1960s: it is covered with tarmac, too much so given the reasonable traffic around it. A renovation project is under way, which should give the square a greener aspect. The main interest is the central fountain (1885) by architect Gaspard André and sculptor Degeorges. The four statues portray Lyon-born artists: painter Hippolyte Fla

voyage.name: Hôtel-Dieu
voyage.hours: Courtyard and gardens: daily 09:00-19:00; shops Mon-Sat 10:30-19:00; cafes Mon-Sat 09:00-19:00
voyage.content: The majestic Hôtel-Dieu was the oldest hospital in Lyon and is one of the largest buildings in Presqu'île. The façade along the river Rhône is over 300 m (984 ft) long. The first hospital was built in 1184-1185; it was modified several times before Soufflot designed the current building, built from 1741 to 1761. The large dome was completed in 1765. The newly built Grange Blanche hospital (today Edouard Herriot) beca

voyage.name: Théâtre des Célestins
voyage.content: Designed by Gaspard André and opened in 1877, the building has a beautiful Italian-style façade. In the middle of the quiet plaza outside the theatre stands a strange periscope in which you can see rotating geometric shapes, like a kaleidoscope. Those were actually painted in the car park beneath the plaza by the famous artist Daniel Buren and they are reflected by a rotating mirror. To enter the car park and see the

voyage.name: Place Bellecour
voyage.content: The largest clear square in Europe. In the centre stands the equestrian statue of Louis XIV ("under the horse's tail" is a usual meeting point for locals). Apart from this, it is rather empty, windy and not so pleasant. A renovation project is under way. Between the southeast corner of Place Bellecour and the river Rhône is Place Antonin Poncet. There was a hospital there (Hôpital de la Charité), built in 1622 and de

voyage.name: Basilica of Saint-Martin d'Ainay
voyage.content: The only entirely Romanesque church in Lyon, dating back to the 11th-12th centuries. The abbey of Ainay was one of the most powerful in France between the 13th and the 16th centuries. A must-see for its very nice atmosphere.

voyage.name: Boat trips on the Saône
voyage.content: A boat trip can be a good way to see Lyon from a different point of view. Boats will take you either upstream to Ile Barbe or downstream to the Confluence. Night trips available on Fridays and Saturdays.

voyage.name: Cité Internationale
voyage.content: This business and residential area in an important urban project for Lyon. Designed by the famous Italian architect Renzo Piano (also known for Beaubourg modern art centre in Paris and part of the Potsdamer Platz area in Berlin), it comprises a convention centre, hotels and luxury apartments just between the Rhône and Parc de la Tête d'Or.

voyage.name: États-Unis neighbourhood
voyage.content: This neighbourhood was built by the famous local architect Tony Garnier in the 1920s to house industry workers. Along with Edouard Herriot hospital, it is one of the masterpieces of this visionary architect. The main axis of the neighbourhood, boulevard des États-Unis, was named to honour the United States, which had just entered World War I when the street was opened in 1917. 25 wall paintings made in the 1980s and

voyage.name: Ile Barbe
voyage.content: This charming island on the river Saône is the only inhabited island in Lyon. In the 5th century, one of the first monasteries in Gaul was founded there. It became a powerful Benedictine abbey (from the 9th century) but was finally ruined in 1526 by Protestants, during the religious wars. Of the three churches that existed on the island, only the Romanesque Notre-Dame remains. The island also has other old buildings

voyage.name: Gratte-Ciel
voyage.address: Cours Émile Zola / avenue Henri Barbusse / place Lazare Goujon, 69100 Villeurbanne
voyage.content: The neighbouring city of Villeurbanne can be seen as the 10th arrondissement because the urban continuity with Lyon is obvious. It has, however, a strong identity of its own. As an industrial town, Villeurbanne has always had a very strong left-wing political inclination. It was governed by the Communist party for the first decades of the 20th century. A strong testimony of this era remains in the form of massive Sov

voyage.name: Palais Saint-Pierre / Musée des Beaux Arts
voyage.price: €6, reduced €4, under 18, EU students, and some others free, audioguide €3 or free for some
voyage.hours: Mon Wed Thu Sat 10:00-18:00, Fri 10:30-18:00, partial closures 12:00-14:15, ticket office closes 17:30

voyage.name: Musée d'Art contemporain
voyage.price: Full price €9; reduced price €6 for people aged 18 to 25 and for holders of a ticket less than 6 months old purchased at the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon; free for under 18s
voyage.content: It holds temporary exhibitions of Contemporary Art, and selections from its permanent collection of more than 1,400 works.

voyage.name: Institut Lumière - Musée vivant du Cinéma
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 11:00-18:30. Closed 1 Jan, 1 May, and 25 Dec. Open on bank holiday Mondays
voyage.content: This museum in the Lumière brothers' house presents an interesting history of cinema through various items and film excerpts. Also worth seeing for the lovely architecture.

voyage.name: Musées Gadagne: Historical museum of Lyon and International puppet museum
voyage.price: 1 museum: €6 including audioguide, 2 museums: €8, 2 museums + temporary exhibition: €10. Under 26 and disabled: free
voyage.address: 14 rue de Gadagne/1 place du Petit Collège
voyage.content: These museums dedicated to the history of the city and to puppets (like the famous Guignol from Lyon). The building is a magnificent Renaissance palace that is worth a visit. A nice garden and cafe have also been created at the top of the building (free access). Unfortunately there is no view, however. Temporary exhibitions are shown. The puppet museum is mostly for kids and is skippable if you don't read French and

voyage.name: Musée urbain Tony Garnier
voyage.price: Guided tours: €6, under 18 €4, children under 5 free; audioguide: €5, under 18 €3, children under 5 free
voyage.hours: Visitor centre: Tue-Sat 14:00-18:00, guided tours Sat at 14:30 or by appointment for groups of 10 or more
voyage.content: This museum was created during the renovation of the États-Unis neighbourhood in the 1980s and 1990s, and the inhabitants were strongly involved in the project. The museum comprises a recreated apartment of the 1930s, which shows how life was like in these very modern housing units, and the 25 wall paintings depicting Garnier's work and ideals. You can also see the walls on your own but you will miss the interesting

voyage.name: Centre d'Histoire de la Résistance et de la Déportation
voyage.alt: Museum of the Resistance during World War II
voyage.content: This museum in the former Gestapo regional headquarters depicts the daily life in Lyon under the German occupation and keeps memories of this tragic period. Often holds exhibitions (mostly photography).

voyage.name: Musée des Arts Décoratifs et Musée des Tissus
voyage.alt: Decorative Arts museum and Fabrics museum
voyage.content: Great if you are into old European oil paintings, or relocated Egyptian, Greek or Mesopotamian antiquities. An impressively large local numismatic gallery. Housed in an interesting building with a pleasant courtyard. Probably disappointing if you have come from larger museums such as those in Paris, unless you have a specific local history or antiquarian focus.

voyage.name: Musée gallo-romain de Fourvière
voyage.price: €4, reduced fee €2.50, under 18 and disabled free; free for all on Th
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, closed 1Jan, 1 May, 1 Nov and 25 Dec
voyage.content: The second largest museum in France, it has all kinds of things relating to Rhone-Alps history. A free visit to the Roman theatres may be just as interesting for those not into the details.

voyage.name: Musée Miniature et Cinéma
voyage.content: Created by artist Dan Ohlmann, this private gallery shows about 120 miniature models of all kinds of scenes: houses, restaurants, workshops, schools, etc., from Lyon or elsewhere, historical or contemporary. The accuracy of the models is astonishing and some sections will be real fun for children. Movie sceneries, models, costumes, masks and props are also presented, including a wand from the Harry Potter films and t

voyage.name: Musée de l'Imprimerie
voyage.content: An excellent collection of some facets of printing. The collection features some particularly early works and a reasonable amount of supporting material. Unfortunately, the collection is quite biased towards local Lyonnaise history and thus coverage of printing as an art remains regrettably rather spotty overall. Minimal coverage of photographic processes, weak coverage of typography, zero technical information about

voyage.name: Musée des Confluences
voyage.content: The spectacular building at the confluence of the Rhône and the Saone is built in a deconstructionist style and has expositions on science and mythology.

voyage.name: Parc de la Tête d'or
voyage.address: Between boulevard des Belges, quai Charles de Gaulle and boulevard de Stalingrad
voyage.content: Completed in 1862, this 105 ha English-style garden is one of the largest and arguably one of the most beautiful urban parks in France. It is a popular place for families as well as joggers. The highlights of the park include the large greenhouses, the botanical garden, the rose garden and the "African plain" in which animals wander in a natural-style environment, perfect for children.

voyage.name: Lyon Zoo
voyage.hours: Nov–Mar: 09:00–17:00 daily; Apr–Oct: 09:00–18:00 daily; May–Sep: 09:00–18:30 daily

voyage.name: Rhône banks
voyage.address: quai Charles de Gaulle, ave de Grande-Bretagne, quai de Serbie, quai Sarrail, quai Augagneur, quai Claude Bernard, ave Leclerc
voyage.content: The right bank of the river Rhône has been turned from an ugly car park into a 5-km promenade with various landscapes and great views over the Croix-Rousse and Presqu'Ile areas. The place had immediate success among locals. A bicycle is perfect to enjoy it.

voyage.name: Parc de Gerland
voyage.content: The Rhône banks promenade ends here. This park does not have the majesty of Parc de la Tête d'Or but it is far less crowded and boasts some nice examples of modern landscaping. Still under development, it should cover 80 hectares when completed.

voyage.name: Saône banks
voyage.address: quai Rambaud, quai Saint-Antoine, quai Gillet
voyage.content: Following the success of the Rhône banks operation, the municipality decided to do renew the operation, this time with the Saône river. The aim is to create a 22km-long promenade between along the Saône banks, separated into two parts (for now): between Confluence and île Barbe, and between the neighboring cities of Fontaines-sur-Saône and Rochetaillée-sur-Saône (north of Lyon). Work is still ongoing but some portion

voyage.name: Parc Sergent Blandan
voyage.address: rue du Repos, rue de l'Epargne, boulevard des Tchécoslovaques
voyage.content: A park built on the grounds of former military barracks. It includes a large skatepark and many sports playgrounds. Still under development, it should cover 17 hectares when completed.

voyage.name: Parc des Hauteurs
voyage.address: place de Fourvière/Montée Nicolas de Lange
voyage.content: This park between the metal tower of Fourvière and the Loyasse cemetery is a promenade with a nice footbridge offering great views towards the Monts d'Or and Beaujolais. There is an aerial adventure course and a skiing and mountain bike slope.

voyage.name: Jardin des Curiosités
voyage.address: Passage des Hauts de St Just
voyage.content: Small garden hidden in the bottom of a street/car park, behind a metallic door. It was designed by Canadian artists in a surrealistic spirit (recalls Magritte or Dali). Also a very nice viewpoint over the southern part of Lyon.

voyage.name: Auditorium
voyage.content: The Lyon National Orchestra plays in this impressive, modern concert hall which also hosts some jazz and world music concerts.

voyage.name: Opera house
voyage.content: The old opera house was completely redesigned by Jean Nouvel in the 1990s and hosts opera and dancing shows, along with a few other concerts (especially jazz) in the smaller "Amphithéâtre" room.

voyage.name: Transbordeur
voyage.content: The medium-sized hall (capacity 1,500) for rock or popular music concerts.

voyage.name: Ninkasi
voyage.content: This is a modern-day institution in Lyon. Ninkasi has two places for live music: Kafé (free shows, essentially electronic music) and Kao (a concert hall dedicated to rock and electronic music). It is also a beer brewery and has bars all over the Presqu'île, and also in Villeurbanne.

voyage.name: Maison de la Danse
voyage.content: A theatre dedicated to modern dancing. Also a fine example of architecture of the 1960s.

voyage.name: Théâtre des Célestins
voyage.content: The historical theatre, in a beautiful 19th century building by Gaspard André. Serious programme.

voyage.name: Théâtre de la Croix-Rousse
voyage.content: 'The other' theatre, with a more avant-garde programme.

voyage.name: TNP
voyage.content: Jean Vilar's spirit of 'popular theatre' lives on in the historically left-wing Villeurbanne.

voyage.name: Théâtre Tête d'Or
voyage.content: This is the only theatre in Lyon showing popular comedies in the Parisian "boulevard" style.

voyage.name: Complexe du Rire
voyage.content: Two rooms and talented young comedians.

voyage.name: Théâtre le Guignol de Lyon
voyage.content: The largest Guignol theatre, showing original creations for children and adults.

voyage.name: Véritable Guignol du Vieux Lyon et du Parc
voyage.hours: Wed Sat Sun, bank and school holidays 15:00, 16:00, 17:00, 18:00
voyage.address: place de Guignol, Parc de la Tête d'Or
voyage.content: Especially intended for children, this outdoor theatre is in the park, near the lake and the zoo.

voyage.name: Institut Lumière
voyage.content: The museum also has a theatre showing thematic series of cinema masterpieces (in original version). The theatre is in the former Lumière factory, which was the scenery of the first movie in history (La sortie des usines Lumière).

voyage.name: Comoedia
voyage.content: After a few years of closure followed by refurbishment works, this independent cinema is now very comfortable and has a relatively avant-garde programme. All foreign movies are shown in original version.

voyage.name: CNP
voyage.address: Bellecour: 12 rue de la Barre; Terreaux: 40 rue du Président Edouard Herriot
voyage.content: Two independent cinemas; the Bellecour branch has the most avant-garde programme. All foreign movies in original version.

voyage.name: Pathé
voyage.content: This major national firm has four theatres in Lyon (Cordeliers, Bellecour, Vaise, Carré de Soie) offering essentially American blockbusters and mainstream French movies. The Bellecour branch has foreign films in original version.

voyage.name: UGC
voyage.content: The other major cinema firm, has four theatres in Lyon (Part-Dieu, Cité Internationale, Astoria, Confluence). The Astoria (M: Masséna) has foreign movies in original version.

voyage.name: Olympique Lyonnais
voyage.address: Parc Olympique Lyonnais, 10 avenue Simone-Veil, Décines-Charpieu
voyage.content: Successful on the soccer field but massively in debt, so OL were relegated in 2025 to Ligue 2, the second tier. The stadium (capacity 59,000) is in the suburb of Décines 15 km east of city centre. The women's team is also badly in debt but continues to play in their top tier.

voyage.name: ASVEL
voyage.content: The Villeurbanne basketball team has a long history as one of the major clubs in the country.

voyage.name: LOU Rugby
voyage.address: Matmut Stadium de Gerland, 353, Avenue Jean-Jaurès
voyage.content: The rugby team of Lyon has bounced between the top two levels of the country's league system (Top 14 and Pro D2) in the 2010s; they have played in Top 14 since 2016–17. The team moved to OL's former home of Stade de Gerland for 2017–18.

voyage.name: Pralus
voyage.content: Chocolatier famed for inventing the Praluline, a decadent, buttery brioche generously studded with pink pralines. There's almost always a line outside, but it moves fast. Even the "petite" (€6.60) serves four. Pralus has other outlets but the Vieux-Lyon branch is the only one open every day.

voyage.name: La Part-Dieu
voyage.content: A huge shopping mall (the largest downtown mall in Europe) on four levels, with most major fashion brands. Avoid Saturday afternoons, the place is awfully crowded.

voyage.name: Rue de la République
voyage.content: This pedestrian street is the main downtown shopping spot. Also check out Rue du Président Edouard Herriot (more expensive in general) and Rue de Brest; these three streets run parallel to each other along Presqu'île.

voyage.name: Rue du Président Edouard Herriot, rue Gasparin, rue Émile Zola, rue des Archers
voyage.content: In the "golden square" between Place Bellecour and Place des Jacobins, you will find a number of famous luxury brands.

voyage.name: Rue Victor Hugo
voyage.content: Brand names and tourist traps south of Bellecour.

voyage.name: Rue Auguste Comte
voyage.content: Parallel to rue Victor Hugo, this is where you will find most antique shops in Lyon.

voyage.name: Carré de Soie
voyage.content: Shopping mall with fashion stores, restaurants and a cinema multiplex, in a developing suburban area.

voyage.name: Confluence
voyage.content: Shopping mall with fashion stores, restaurants and a cinema multiplex, in a new area.

voyage.name: Halles de Lyon Paul Bocuse
voyage.content: The Halles moved to the Part-Dieu area in 1971. If you want the very best food, this is the place to go. It has a price however.

voyage.name: Croix-Rousse market
voyage.content: Very popular and typical market mith many local producers. On Tuesdays, also sells non-food items. Very crowded on sunny Sundays, but this is the right time to enjoy the particular mood of the neighbourhood.

voyage.name: St Antoine Market
voyage.address: Quai St Antoine and Quai des Célestins
voyage.content: The other major market, in a wealthier part of town. Also some local fruit and vegetable producers. Eating oysters by the Saône is a very pleasant occupation before Sunday lunch.

voyage.name: Bahadourian
voyage.content: A large Oriental shop, with all kinds of exotic foods, especially North African. In the heart of the picturesque Guillotière neighbourhood.

voyage.name: Antic Wine
voyage.content: This tiny shop has an exceptional selection of wines from all over the world. Very interesting selection of Rhône valley wines, amazing collection of old Burgundies. Very reasonable prices. Also a must-see for port amateurs, with the largest selection in France and prices ranging from €12 to €3,000.

voyage.name: Vercoquin
voyage.content: This wine store is specialised in organic and "natural" wines. It is also a wine bar, all bottles of the shop can be drunk there with a price supplement of €6.

voyage.name: Chez Mounier
voyage.content: A traditional bouchon (restaurant) with good food.

voyage.name: Chez M'man
voyage.content: French cuisine, typical Lyonnais dishes and excellent hospitality. It's a well-run establishment near Place Bellecour. A picturesque place in an endearing environment.

voyage.name: Pitaya Thaï Street Food
voyage.content: A dive into the streets of Bangkok and its colourful and tasty street food. Fresh and quality products cooked in the wok at the moment in front of your eyes. Delicious and generous dishes.

voyage.name: Boulangerie Chez Jules St Paul
voyage.content: Small boulangerie near the historic centre with a great variety of breads, cakes, sandwiches, pizza, salads. There is also the possibility to sit down. Very good croissant aux almond. Also nice to have breakfast. Warm welcome.

voyage.name: La Piazzetta
voyage.content: Nice setting on the banks of the Saône, the owner's cooking is a delight. Like a trip to Italy. Quality ingredients, the pastas and pizzas are excellent and the portions generous. Fresh products decorate the pasta and pizzas according to the seasons.

voyage.name: Taco Taco
voyage.content: Very good and a big variety of tacos, burritos and quesadillas as well as toppings and sauces to choose from ranging from mild to spicy. Everything is freshly prepared in front of the customer. The burritos are different than from the big Mexican fast food chains and as it is more authentic here.

voyage.name: Nardone
voyage.hours: Summer: daily 09:00-01:00; winter: Wed-Sun 10:00-19:00, closed Dec 31-Mar 10
voyage.address: 3 place Ennemond Fousseret/26 quai de Bondy,
voyage.content: Delicious ice cream with very original flavours, served on a very pleasant terrace. Completely overcrowded on sunny weekends, be prepared to queue... but it is worth the wait if you are a real ice cream fan.

voyage.name: Boulangerie du Palais
voyage.content: In this small bakery, you will find good praline tarts, a popular local dessert.

voyage.name: La Vieille Canaille
voyage.content: A typical French restaurant where the atmosphere is friendly. You will enjoy the large range of wine, the menu explanation and wine suggestions of the waiter. English speaking/menu in English - Terrace in summer.

voyage.name: Wallace Bar
voyage.content: This nice pub is a good spot for drinks and live sports, but also serves good British and French food in large portions.

voyage.name: Bouchon Chez Paul
voyage.content: A very good bouchon serving huge portions. Noisy and friendly.

voyage.name: Le Layon
voyage.hours: Daily lunch and dinner. Serves all day (12:00-00:00) on Sat and Sun
voyage.content: In another street full of tourist traps, this restaurant offers very good, classical local and French cuisine. Try the grenouilles (frogs). Very nice terrace. Good wine list at interesting prices.

voyage.name: Les Adrets
voyage.content: Very good classic French cuisine, made from quality products, in a nice decor.

voyage.name: Le Potager des Halles
voyage.price: If you want cheaper but just as good, try Le Bistrot du Potager next door, where the same owners serve Spanish-style tapas which are a great value for money (no reservations)
voyage.content: This restaurant serves traditional French cuisine made from very good and very fresh products, with a Mediterranean influence. The chocolate fondant dessert is amazing. Very good wine list too. The lunch menu is an absolute steal.

voyage.name: Balthaz'Art
voyage.content: Croix-Rousse has more and more interesting restaurants, and this one is a fine example. In a "flea-market-meets-art-gallery" decor, you will enjoy a fresh and creative cuisine with Mediterranean and Asian influences. Nice wine list, and it is still possible to get a table at a relatively short notice.

voyage.name: L'Art et la Manière
voyage.content: Small no-tourist restaurant in a no-tourist area. Friendly yet professional service, short menu but very creative, high-quality cooking. Good (although short) wine list. The best bottles are at amazingly low prices given their "constant mark-up" policy.

voyage.name: Brasserie Georges
voyage.content: An exceptional traditional brasserie, serving both traditional Lyonnaise food as well as Alsatian favorites like the Choucroute Impériale, a huge pile of sauerkraut with various sausages and an entire pork knuckle. The cavernous main dining hall is a real Art Deco treat. Founded in 1836, this is one of the largest brasseries in France and it can serve 1000 people a night over two sittings. Reservations accepted only

voyage.name: L'Ouest
voyage.content: A brasserie owned by Paul Bocuse, near the river Saône. The specialities are fish and cuisine of the Caribbean.

voyage.name: Paul Bocuse
voyage.content: The home base of the master of all chefs, "Monsieur Paul", this restaurant held 3 Michelin stars for a record 55 years, dropping to two only after his death in 2018. Classic French cuisine, with an extortionate price tag; by all accounts the food remains very good, but there are definitely cheaper options around.

voyage.name: Au 14 Février
voyage.content: If you can book at least two months in advance and are ready for a "surprise" menu, this tiny place (16 seats!) run by Japanese chef Tsuyoshi Arai is a rather unique experience. Just tell your waiter what you don't like or can't eat, and you will be served a five- or nine-course menu that changes every day. The cuisine is French with Japanese hints, amazingly creative, and most importantly delicious.

voyage.name: La Mère Brazier — Mathieu Viannay
voyage.content: The restaurant, opened in 1921 by the legendary Eugénie Brazier, was taken over by the talented young chef Mathieu Viannay and awarded 2 stars by the Michelin guide only a few months after its opening. Revisited all-time classics (Bresse poultry with truffles, artichokes with foie gras).

voyage.name: Têtedoie
voyage.content: A new address for a well-recognized chef. The previous restaurant had a classic dining room on the banks of the Saône. Têtedoie is now taking his restaurant to the next level with a prestigious location offering one of the best views in town and a very contemporary decor, with the same culinary spirit and prices. The wine list is so big they have to carry it around on a trolley. The place also features a wine bar, a

voyage.name: Prairial
voyage.content: Modern, inventive Michelin-starred haute cuisine, served only as a degustation set menu: the 5-course "Confluence" (€99, lunch only) or the full 8-course "Prairial" (€135). Expect local, seasonal produce, heavy on vegetables and seafood and light on meat, with amazing sauces often made from fermented ingredients. Reservations essential. Dinner seatings W-Su at 20:00, lunch F Sa at 12:00.

voyage.name: Kelly's Pub
voyage.content: Irish pub, live music on Saturday, Irish music sessions on Thursday, quiz every Monday, pool, darts, Irish and English pub food, air conditioning.

voyage.name: Paddy's Corner
voyage.content: Perfect little pub in the Croix-Rousse area, off the beaten track. Live music sessions every Thursday, Pub Quiz on Tuesdays.

voyage.name: Johnny Walsh's
voyage.content: Nice, authentic Irish pub with good music and some live performances.

voyage.name: Wallace
voyage.content: Comfortable beer and whisky bar with a nice terrace, live sports, pub quiz on Thursdays.

voyage.name: The Smoking Dog
voyage.content: English pub. Pub quiz on Tuesdays. Air conditioning.

voyage.name: Hot Club de Lyon
voyage.content: Jazz club (since 1948), in an old typical cellar, with good live jazz 5 nights/week.

voyage.name: L'Abreuvoir
voyage.content: There you can join some crazy French listening to crazy French music. Definitely an experience, though not everyone's cup of tea.

voyage.name: Le Perroquet Bourré
voyage.content: Cheap rum, the inside is decorated as a pirate ship.

voyage.name: Le Fruit Defendu
voyage.content: A great little hole-in-the-wall bar, good for beers and cocktails, and a great place to start the night! Try the Stella with a shot of orange liquor!

voyage.name: Sirius
voyage.content: Live events almost every day of the week. On weekends, there are two dancefloors with all kinds of music. No dress code! Nice.

voyage.name: Q-Boat
voyage.content: Another boat, here the hype crowd will feel at home.

voyage.name: Marquise
voyage.content: Quai Augagneur. Here you get nice alternative hip-hop, retro soul, etc. Sometimes theatre performances.

voyage.name: La Cave des Voyageurs
voyage.content: Opened over 20 years ago by "Jeannot", the picturesque and loud-mouthed owner of the other bar next door, this small and friendly wine bar has built a wide and interesting selection of several hundred wines over the years. Of course the locals are well represented (Beaujolais, Burgundy, Rhône valley) but the list also keeps expanding geographically. Also serves some quality food: ham, sausages, cheese.

voyage.name: Goudyvins
voyage.content: A few steps away from the busy Place Bellecour, a new friendly place where you can enjoy both local and foreign wines with prices starting at €5-7 for a glass of either "blanc", "rosé", or "rouge". The selection is actually quite wide so ask for recommendations, the owner is always helpful and will help you choose your little treat following your tastes. In summer, you definitely need to be lucky to find a spot on th

voyage.name: Georges Five
voyage.price: Wine by the glass from €3, bottles €18-€3,000
voyage.content: This place was opened by the owner of the wine shop Antic Wine. It has therefore a very wide selection of wines (2,800 references), ranging from small local producers to the most famous and sought-after names. Also top-quality food: ham, cheese, etc. Be careful: the place is small, always packed and hosts numerous private events, so if you haven't made your reservation a couple of weeks in advance, save yourself the

voyage.name: Vercoquin
voyage.content: See "Buy".

voyage.name: Hôtel Vaubecour
voyage.content: Clean, quiet and friendly hotel with small bedroom and modern bathroom. No air conditioning.

voyage.name: Auberge de Jeunesse de Vieux Lyon
voyage.content: Belongs to YHA (international youth hostels association). Bunk bed in a dorm, plus breakfast for €21 (plus fee, if not member of YHA). Excellent views over city. Tiny kitchen, extremely limited rooms for couples/families. No telephone bookings.

voyage.name: Camping des Barolles
voyage.price: e.g. One adult/one child/one tent/one car = €19 (June 2016)
voyage.address: 88, Avenue Maréchal Foch, 69230 Saint Genis Laval
voyage.content: Campsite caters for camper vans, chalets and free camping. There is a small shop at reception. It is a couple of minutes' drive from a large shopping centre. To get to Lyon by public transport, take bus 78 to Oullins and then change to the metro. Friendly staff. Free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Citadines Part-Dieu Lyon
voyage.content: Housing 98 flats over 7 floors, varying from studios to one-bedrooms; Each apartment has a bathroom with a hairdryer, a separate kitchen area, TV with satellite channels and a direct-line phone.

voyage.name: Hotel Victoria
voyage.content: This place is unpretentious and satisfactory. Reasonable value accommodation in a handy location with a friendly welcome.

voyage.name: Hotel Saint Paul
voyage.content: This 2-star hotel offers rather small rooms but very good service and cleanliness. Good value for money. The street can be quite noisy, so ask for a room on the courtyard side or bring your earplugs.

voyage.name: NH Lyon Aéroport
voyage.content: 245 modern rooms and Nhube restaurant, meeting rooms and a spa.

voyage.name: LaTour-Lyon
voyage.content: An accommodation in a renaissance tower in Vieux-Lyon. A delightful duplex and unique setting with a panoramic view through 17 windows and luxurious amenities.

voyage.name: Hôtel Mercure Lyon Centre Château Perrache
voyage.address: 12 cours de Verdun Rambaud, Esplanade de la gare

voyage.name: Hotel Sofitel Lyon Bellecour
voyage.content: Luxury hotel with a large number of meeting rooms for conventions.

voyage.name: Collège Hôtel
voyage.content: This 3-star hotel is decorated in the manner of an early 20th century school.

voyage.name: Cour des Loges
voyage.content: In an exceptional 14th-century building.

voyage.name: Le Royal Hotel Lyon
voyage.content: Perfectly perched on Place Bellecour since 1888, this rather over-the-top hotel is now part of Accor's boutiquey MGallery collection. Expect rococo and chinoiserie, creepy marionettes, a bar encrusted in red velvet that could double as a Parisian bordello, and compact but modern and comfortable rooms.

voyage.name: Car museum of Rochetaillée
voyage.price: Fees: Adults €5, free for children under 18
voyage.hours: Open Tue-Sun 09:00-19:00 in July and August, Tue-Sun 09:00-18:00 the rest of the year. Closed on Christmas and New Year
voyage.content: Has a very nice collection of modern and old cars. The main attraction of the museum is Adolf Hitler's armored car.
